test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: There are two classrooms A and B having a certain number of students. If 5 students are shifted from A to B, then B has twice the number of students as A. If 1 student is sent from B to A, then both classrooms will have the same number of students. How many students are there in B?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the number of students in **Class A** be A and **Class B** be B.

From the second condition: If 1 student goes from B to A, they become equal ⇒ **B − 1 = A + 1** ⇒ **B − A = 2**.

Check options for **B**: If B = 19, then A = 17.

Verify first condition: If 5 shift from A to B, A becomes 17 − 5 = 12, and B becomes 19 + 5 = 24.

Since 24 is **twice** of 12, the condition is satisfied.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8ac63ce07f1385157e7438216d31e6a2a4c99e54ff28cb8af9e4b6fac26e3588.png] 

Let **Class A** have x students and **Class B** have y students.

**Case 1:** 5 students shifted from A to B.

⇒ 2(x − 5) = y + 5

⇒ 2x − 10 = y + 5 ⇒ 2x − y = 15 --- (Eq. 1)

**Case 2:** 1 student sent from B to A.

⇒ x + 1 = y − 1

⇒ y − x = 2 ⇒ x = y − 2 --- (Eq. 2)

Substitute x in Eq. 1:

⇒ 2(y − 2) − y = 15

⇒ 2y − 4 − y = 15

⇒ y = 19

**∴ The correct answer is 19 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

These problems are solved by translating **word conditions** into algebraic equations of the form ax + by = c.

Substitution Method

Expressing one variable in terms of the other from the **simpler equation** and substituting it into the more complex one to find the value.

Elimination Method

Multiplying equations by suitable constants so that adding or subtracting them **eliminates one variable**.</p
